new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File (18 pp., J-STAGE publisher PDF) opened; extracted text per page plus rendered images (150 dpi) of PDF pp.2-5 = printed pp.159-162. Printed p.161, last line, reads exactly 「強勢（ストレス）は，一般に語末にくる。」 and printed p.162 opens 「例：papús《肺臓》，taǰyák《星》 / wacák《小牛》 masík《ひたい》 / mayák《月，太陰》」 with the acute accents visible on the page image (the text layer drops them); after the initial/final cluster paragraphs p.162 continues 「母音の長短は音韻的機能を持っていないように思われる。」 and then the undecided tone discussion (dår 'mountain' vs dår 'wood'). So the quote, locator and translation are correct; the '[..]' elides only the consonant-cluster lists. I checked one possible confound: forms written with a raised vertical stroke…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress in Kordar (Kurdar) Pashai generally falls on the final syllable; all cited examples are disyllables accented on the last vowel. Hedged with 'generally'; no conditioning by vowel length stated (length judged non-phonemic in this dialect), unlike Grjunberg's pan-Pashai 'last long vowel' formulation.
new_statements.exceptions: None listed; the hedge 一般に ('generally') implies unlisted exceptions. Author separately notes an unresolved possible tone contrast (dâr 'mountain' rising vs dâr 'wood' level/falling) from de-aspiration, undecided for Kordar.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level statement based on elicited citation forms (Hattori basic-vocabulary list) from a single Kordar-born speaker interviewed in Kabul, Dec 1966-Jan 1967; preliminary report.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statement describes the Kordar (Kurdar) dialect, Glottolog kurd1258, which Glottolog 5.x files as a dialect of Northeast Pashayi nort2666 (classification chain verified via glottolog.org JSON: pash1270 > east2322 > nort2666 > kurd1258); Nawata himself (p.159) assigns Kordar to Morgenstierne's Northeastern group, closest to Areti-Kandak. Data from one speaker recorded in Kabul, not in situ. Grjunberg 1999's 'last long vowel' rule is a pan-Pashai (pash1270-level) statement, not NE-specific.

sources.note: p.161 (sec. IV phonology): stress (sutoresu) generally comes at word end; p.162 examples papús, taǰyák, wacák, masík, mayák (all final-accented); vowel length apparently not phonemic; possible tone contrast (dâr 'mountain' vs dâr 'wood') left undecided for Kordar. Kordar = Kurdar (Glottolog kurd1258, dialect of nort2666); p.159 places it in Morgenstierne's Northeastern group, closest to Areti-Kandak.
